messages:
maya: Quick Q — I'm trying to wire secrets into the service Helm chart. I want the secret name to be derived from the release (e.g. '{{ .Release.Name }}-secrets') but when I put that string in values.yaml and reference it as `{{ .Values.database.secretName }}` the template is not evaluated and ends up literally containing the braces. Is there a recommended pattern to evaluate templates stored in values.yaml?

devin: Use `tpl`. It evaluates strings in values as templates with a given context. Example in your Deployment template:```yaml
env:
  - name: DB_PASS
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: {{ tpl .Values.database.secretName . }}
        key: password
```
And in values.yaml:```yaml
database:
  secretName: "{{ .Release.Name }}-db"
```
That will render to `myrelease-db` at template render time.

lucy: Quick note: `tpl` runs at template render time (Helm templating), not runtime in k8s. Also be careful about user-provided values containing templates — validate/escape as needed.

sam: Another pattern is to avoid templates in values and use chart helpers to build names, e.g. in _helpers.tpl:```gotemplate
{{- define "mychart.secretName" -}}
{{ printf "%s-%s" (include "mychart.fullname" .) "secrets" }}
{{- end -}}
```
Then in your manifest:```yaml
name: {{ include "mychart.secretName" . }}
```
This keeps logic in templates rather than values.

lucy: Also, decide between `envFrom: secretRef:` vs explicit `secretKeyRef:`. `envFrom` brings all keys into env, which is convenient but noisier and couples to secret structure. For single keys, use secretKeyRef. Example explicit form:```yaml
env:
- name: API_KEY
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: {{ tpl .Values.api.secretName . }}
      key: api_key
```
Example envFrom:```yaml
envFrom:
- secretRef:
    name: {{ tpl .Values.api.secretName . }}
```

devin: If you need to template a map of envs from values (like setting multiple envs via values.yaml) you can combine `toYaml` + `tpl`, e.g.:```gotemplate
{{- $envs := tpl (toYaml .Values.extraEnv) . | fromYaml -}}
{{- range $k, $v := $envs }}
- name: {{ $k }}
  value: {{ $v | quote }}
{{- end }}
```
But be careful: that will evaluate templates in string values inside `extraEnv`.

maya: Got it — thanks. One follow-up: does `tpl` need the second argument to be `.`? I tried `tpl .Values.something` without passing `.` and it failed.

devin: Yes, `tpl` signature is `tpl TEMPLATE_STRING CONTEXT`. Pass `.` to give it the chart context. So use `tpl .Values.someName .`.

sam: Also FYI, for secrets created by ExternalSecret/SealedSecrets, the secret name may not be tied to release name. If ops creates them externally, prefer to reference an explicit global value like `global.externalSecrets.dbName`.
